items.prompt: Which hand tells the hours?
items.description: A clock has a short thick orange hand and a long thin blue hand.
options: Both hands do the same job
items.explanation: Hours use the short hand. The hands have different jobs.

items.prompt: Read this clock.
items.description: Short hand at 8; long hand at 12.
items.explanation: The long hand at twelve means zero minutes past. Read the short hand for the hour.

items.prompt: How many minutes past does the long hand show?
items.description: Long hand at 4.
items.explanation: 4 groups of five make 20 minutes.

items.prompt: How many minutes past does the long hand show?
items.description: Long hand at 10.
items.explanation: 10 groups of five make 50 minutes past. The question asks for minutes past.

items.prompt: Which phrase matches this clock?
items.description: Long hand at 6; short hand halfway from 4 to 5.
items.explanation: Half past is thirty minutes after the hour that has started.

items.prompt: Which phrase matches this clock?
items.description: Long hand at 9; short hand between 8 and 9, closer to 9.
items.explanation: Forty-five minutes have passed. Fifteen remain until the next hour: quarter to the next hour.

items.prompt: Read the hour and minutes together.
items.description: Short hand just after 5; long hand at 2.
items.explanation: Read the hour the short hand has passed. Count five minutes for each number reached by the long hand.

items.prompt: Read the hour and minutes together.
items.description: Short hand between 11 and 12; long hand at 8.
items.explanation: The short hand moves continuously. The approaching hour has not started yet.

items.prompt: Which pieces belong to the whole strip?
items.description: One outlined strip with five equal parts; 2 shaded.
items.explanation: The whole includes both shaded and unshaded pieces inside the border.

items.prompt: A strip is cut into five pieces. One piece is much larger than the others. Are these equal parts?
items.description: No picture is needed.
options: Yes, because they came from one strip
Yes, because we can count them
No, the pieces must be the same size
items.explanation: Equal parts of one whole must have equal size, not just belong to the same strip.

items.prompt: In 3/7, what does the bottom number 7 tell us?
items.description: Read the fraction in the question.
options: Seven equal parts make the whole
items.explanation: The denominator counts all equal parts in one whole. The numerator counts selected parts.

items.prompt: What fraction of the whole is shaded?
items.description: One whole with five equal large parts; 3 shaded.
items.explanation: Count all five equal parts below the line and the selected parts above it.

items.prompt: Which fraction equals 2/6?
items.description: Use the same whole.
items.explanation: Divide both numerator and denominator by two. The amount stays the same.

items.prompt: Which fraction equals 3/9?
items.description: Use the same whole.
items.explanation: Group each three ninths into a third. Divide both counts by three.

items.prompt: For the same-sized whole, which is larger: 1/5 or 1/10?
items.description: Both fractions refer to identical whole sizes.
items.explanation: Dividing the same whole into more equal pieces makes each piece smaller.

items.prompt: These wholes are identical. Which shaded amount is larger?
items.description: Two equal-sized wholes divided into seven equal parts each. Top: 2 selected; bottom: 5 selected.
items.explanation: With the same whole and denominator, more selected parts means a larger fraction.
